title: mxv/down/v1
description: The processes that the run stopped, in the order it stopped them, and a failure for each process group that outlived SIGKILL.

dry_run.description: Present, and true, when the run was a dry run that changed nothing.

data.description: The rows for the ids that worked, in the order the caller gave the ids.

failures.description: The failures of the ids that did not work. It is empty when every id worked.

items.description: A failure of some of the ids: the fields of the failure document without schema.

url.description: A page that explains the failure. It is present only when the failure has one.

key.description: The key that the caller gave for the answer that failed, when the failure is one answer of a batch.

index.description: The position of key among the keys that the caller gave, counted from 0, so two failures of the same key differ. It is present only with key.

code.description: The failure's stable code in the tool's spelling, such as shelf::books::not_found. It is one or more printable ASCII characters without spaces, from ! to ~.

cause.description: The errors that led to the failure, joined with ": ". It is present only when the failure has a cause.

fields.description: The values at fault, in the order the failure gives them, each under a name of one or more lowercase ASCII letters, digits and underscores. A value is a string, an integer, a boolean, null, or an array or object of such values, and an object holds each key once. It is present only when the failure names at least one.

labels.description: The places in a source, such as a file, that the failure points at, in the order the failure gives them. It is present only when the failure has at least one label.

offset.description: The byte offset of the start of the span from the start of the source.

length.description: The length of the span in bytes.

name.description: The name of the source, such as a file name. It is present only when the span could be read and the source has a name.

line.description: The 1-based line that holds the start of the span. It is present only when the span could be read.

column.description: The 1-based column of the start of the span, counted in characters of its line. It is present only when the span could be read.

excerpt.description: The lines of the source that the span covers, with one line before and one after where the source has them. It is present only when the span could be read.

line.description: The 1-based number of the first line of the excerpt.

text.description: The lines, joined by the line breaks of the source, without a line break at the end.
What the label says about the span. It is present only when the label has text.

related.description: The diagnostics that the failure's diagnostic relates to it, in the order it gives them. It is present only when there is at least one.

code.description: The related diagnostic's own code, which is free text. It is present only when the diagnostic has one.

severity.description: How severe the related diagnostic is. A diagnostic that gives no severity is an error.

cause.description: The errors below the related diagnostic, joined with ": ". It is present only when there is one.

What the label says about the span. It is present only when the label has text.

help.description: The related diagnostic's advice. It is present only when it gives some.

url.description: A page that explains the related diagnostic. It is present only when it has one.

related.description: The diagnostics related to this one, in the same shape, to at most eight levels below the failure.

recovery.description: What the caller can do next, tagged by kind.

oneOf.description: Run this command. With `all`, run it once with every value of the failure's field that `all` names in place of the argument's placeholder, such as `<ID>...`.

alternatives.description: Other repairs the caller can try, in order of preference, each in the shape of recovery. It is present only when the failure offers at least one.

items.description: A repair the caller can try instead, tagged by kind.

ProcessRow.description:
One process or container of a workspace, as `up`, `down`, `restart`
and `status` print it.

name.description: The process's or container's name in the manifest.

state.description:
`running`, `exited` when it ended on its own or something other
than `mxv down` stopped it, `created` for a container that docker
created and did not start, `stopped`, `starting` while it is not
ready yet, `stopping`, `restarting` while docker restarts a
container, or `unknown` when mxv cannot tell.

ready.description:
Whether the process has been ready since it last started: true
once its readiness check passed, or once a process without one
outlasted its start grace, and false while it runs and has not,
such as after its keeper or docker restarted it. It is null when it
does not run, and for a process that mxv started before phase ran
its processes.

pid.description:
The process id, which is also its process group's id, while a
process runs, and null for a container.

code.description:
The exit code of an exited process, or null when a signal ended it
or it has not exited. A container's code is the one docker reports,
such as 137 for a container that SIGKILL ended.

signal.description:
The number of the signal that ended an exited process, such as 15
for SIGTERM, or null.

reason.description:
Why mxv cannot tell the state of an `unknown` process, or why it
does not know the exit code of an exited process that an earlier
version of mxv started, such as one whose group SIGKILL ended
before its shell wrote the exit file, or null when it knows.

group_alive.description:
Whether the process group of an exited process that an earlier
version of mxv started still has a member, such as a child it
started in the background, which `mxv down` stops. It is null while
the process runs, and for every process that phase runs, because
phase stops what is left of a process's group when the process
ends.

ports.description:
The ports that a process receives, as `VARIABLE=port`, or that a
container publishes, as `port-name=port`.

log.description:
The process's log file, which `mxv logs` prints, or null for a
container, whose output docker keeps and `mxv logs` also prints.

sandbox.description:
Whether phase runs a host process under its sandbox, as phase
describes it: `seatbelt (partial: <what it leaves open>)` on macOS,
or `unsandboxed (<reason>)`, such as `unsandboxed (its app declares
no permissions)` for a process whose manifest has no `permissions`
table. It is null for a container and for a process that phase
does not run.

notes.description:
What `up` and `restart` found about the process beside its state:
a warning when the process's running container still has its
earlier secret files, because `up` could not rewrite them, and an
info line when `up` rewrote them. Every other command prints none.

KindName.description: Whether a row is a process or a container.

oneOf.description: A process that mxv starts on the host.
A container that mxv runs with docker.

StateName.description: The state of a process, as a row prints it.

oneOf.description: The process runs.
The process ended.
docker created the container and did not start it.
The process is not started.
The process started and is not ready yet.
The process is stopping.
docker is restarting the container.
mxv cannot tell the process's state.

NoteRow.description:
Something that `up` or `restart` found about a process, as its row
prints it.

level.description: `warning` when something did not happen as asked, or `info`.

message.description: phase's sentence, which names the process and holds no value.

oneOf.description:
Something did not happen as asked, such as a rewrite of secret
files that failed.

Something happened that the person may want to know, such as a
rewrite of secret files.
